svg.title: BIO-MOUSE prototype wiring guide based on the supplied component diagram
svg.desc: The supplied prototype image is shown as a component reference. Verified power and signal connections are listed separately for the Arduino Uno, L298N, LM2596, ESP32-CAM, sensors, buzzer, and whisker switches.
svg.text: BIO-MOUSE — PROTOTYPE WIRING GUIDE
Component picture supplied by you, with a readable connection schedule based on the prototype pin map.
COMPONENT REFERENCE IMAGE
The colored lines in the source sketch cross and are not used as the wiring authority; follow the connection lists on this page.
1. POWER — CONNECT WITH POWER OFF
7.4 V motor battery and switch
Battery + → switch → split to L298N “12V / Vs” and LM2596 IN+.
Battery − → L298N GND and LM2596 IN−.
LM2596 OUT+ → ESP32-CAM 5V pin, after setting output to 5.0 V.
LM2596 OUT− → common GND; ESP32-CAM GND connects here too.
Arduino UNO and breadboard rails
Separate 9 V supply → UNO DC jack or VIN; its − goes to UNO GND.
UNO 5V → breadboard + rail; UNO GND → breadboard − rail.
Join that − rail to the same common GND as battery − and LM2596 OUT−.
IMPORTANT POWER CHECKS
Keep the 7.4 V, UNO 9 V, and regulated 5 V positive rails separate.
Never connect LM2596 IN+ to UNO 5V. Never feed 9 V into UNO 5V.
Measure LM2596 OUT before attaching the ESP32-CAM; set it to 5.0 V.
Use the L298N 5V terminal only as specified for your exact board/jumper setup.
Check that the motors and battery are suitable for the L298N and 7.4 V pack.
2. L298N AND MOTORS
UNO D10 → ENA (remove ENA jumper)
UNO D5 → ENB (remove ENB jumper)
UNO D9 → IN1; D8 → IN2
UNO D7 → IN3; D6 → IN4
OUT1/OUT2 → one motor pair; OUT3/OUT4 → other pair.
L298N GND → battery − and common GND.
Lift the wheels for first tests. If one side turns backward, swap that motor pair’s two output wires.
3. UNO SENSORS AND SWITCHES
AMG8833: SDA → A4; SCL → A5
HC-SR04: TRIG → D4; ECHO → D11
Left microswitch: NO → D2; COM → GND
Right microswitch: NO → D3; COM → GND
Active buzzer signal → A3; use a transistor driver if needed.
Sensor grounds → common GND; power from 5V only if the breakout allows it.
Whisker inputs use INPUT_PULLUP; leave NC unconnected. No physical E-STOP is fitted.
4. ESP32-CAM SERIAL LINK
ESP32-CAM GPIO13 TX → UNO D0 / RX
UNO D1 / TX → level shifter/divider → GPIO14 RX
ESP32-CAM GND ↔ common GND
Do not feed 5 V UNO TX directly into ESP32-CAM RX.
Disconnect D0/D1 wires when uploading firmware to the UNO.
GPIO13/14 overlap microSD pins; leave microSD unused in this wiring.
The link must match the ESP32-CAM firmware serial pin configuration.
BATTERY MONITOR NOTE
The firmware’s A0 divider thresholds currently assume a 3S battery, while this prototype uses a 7.4 V (2S) pack. Leave the divider disconnected until the firmware thresholds are corrected.
Power off before rewiring. Verify polarity and continuity. This map describes intended connections; confirm actual module labels and ratings.
